scope: Acceptance requirements; real database and cross-backend execution remain outstanding

cases.description: Valid refresh cookie and JSON or URL-encoded body each revoke the matching session, clear both cookies and return the success envelope.
Without refresh, valid access cookie or strictly formatted Bearer header revokes the matching current session.
Invalid nonempty refresh wins over valid body and access; whitespace-only refresh cookie suppresses body but falls back to access.
Invalid nonempty access cookie wins over valid Bearer; bare Authorization is not a Bearer credential.
Absent, expired, wrong-signature, wrong-type and stale credentials leave all sessions unchanged and return success with cleared cookies when database lifecycle succeeds.
A valid JWT can revoke a matching session with expired database timestamps; a mismatched user, session, hash or access jti cannot revoke it.
Storage error returns a safe failure with no new cookie changes; closing after a committed update may leave the session revoked despite the failure.
Logout first makes a competing refresh fail; refresh first makes logout using the old refresh return success without revoking the rotated session.
Allowed and rejected CORS preflight occurs without session storage access.
With shared keys and isolated Oracle, each backend revokes tokens issued by each backend; Nuxt Web and Flutter observe subsequent authenticated requests fail.
